summary: Daily sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan with setter Kim Forbes-Sobers and new closer Richard Claessen, which then continues as a one-to-one call review after Kim drops. The first section covers Richard's first close, which was not the $6,000 programme but a 'Primal University' downsell at $200/month; Chris presses him on why he did not run an open-wallet before accepting the prospect's word that he could not afford 6K, and walks through the Primal U price ladder. Projections are set for Richard (2 units / 8K this week, then 3-4, then 1) and Kim's setting metrics are reviewed (pickup rate down, ~25 sets/week, 5-unit projection held). The second half is a detailed review of Richard's first sales call with a San Francisco prospect, covering call opening, discovery order, handling a trust objection early, the guarantee, and pitching the nutrition pillar.
notable: An undisclosed lower-price product, 'Primal University', is in active use as a downsell: $200/month (~$2,400/yr), $2,000 paid up front for 12 months, and '$4K for three months'. Richard closed his first deal on the $200/month tier.

Primal University closes are excluded from the units and cash-collected projections but still counted as closes: 'it counts as a clothes, you can count it, but you can't put it on a unit for the projections... don't fill it in'. Rep comp is '50 bucks for every $200 monthly'.
Chris states Harry Edmonds was previously banned from selling the downsell after using it to avoid working price objections: 'Harry, you're no longer allowed to sell Primal University.'

Guarantee handling: Chris confirms a guarantee exists but coaches deflecting it — 'yes, we do have a guarantee, but what in life is actually guaranteed?' and 'it's only guaranteed for people who actually follow through and put in the work.' Richard's takeaway: 'I should always have in my background that we never have a guarantee.'

Chris instructs that the nutrition pillar must be pitched to every prospect regardless of their actual diet: 'Your job is to figure out how to make pillar two match them because they wouldn't be here if there wasn't something up with their nutrition.'
Standing instruction: 'If it ever comes down to price, always open wallet.'
Stated benchmarks: team close rate '25 to 30%', show rate ~75%, Andrew Musial 'closing about 35%, 40%'; Chris tells Richard he can close 40-50%.
Kettlebell shipping was discontinued: 'if somebody lived in the US, we used to send them a kettlebell to start, but we can't do it anymore.'
Claims used in the trust rebuttal: 'we've worked with like 1200 clients' and Trevor's following given as both 1.3 million and 1.2 million in the same role-play.
Chris advises Richard to start swinging kettlebells so he can truthfully answer prospects who ask whether he trains with them, explicitly rejecting lying: 'I don't ever recommend lying to people.'
A booked call was cancelled as a wrong number and logged as bad data; the SalesKick bot had continued messaging the contact after they said wrong number.
